clue.text: Spot golfer about to receive kiss

indicators.note: to receive means the turned name holds the kiss inside it
about signals that the golfer's name is turned round

parts.note: Ernie Els is the South African golfer
a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: A golfer is spotted leaning in to kiss someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Els is a crossword favourite among golfers; 'about' turns his name round to SLE before 'to receive' wraps it round the kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mark or spot on a surface is a fleck, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Each person is fitted with one in old age

parts.note: per means each, as in ten pounds per head

indicators.note: is fitted with means the word for person has the numeral for one placed inside it

parts.note: man is used for a person in general
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Every person gets fitted with something once they reach old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old age' is not about elderly people: an age is a span of geological time.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists name a period of the Palaeozoic era after Perm in Russia; an age here is a span of Earth's history.

clue.text: Police do wrong to arrest unionist, is the general view

indicators.note: to arrest means the jumble seizes and holds the unionist letter inside it
wrong signals that the letters of police do are jumbled

explanation.surface: Officers act improperly in detaining a trade unionist, and that is the general opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges POLICEDO into COPDOEIL, and 'to arrest' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for a quick glance that takes in a whole scene, so a comprehensive general view.

clue.text: From shelf, take book

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove a volume from the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'take' comes from the old prescription heading Recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: An accounts book in which a business records its transactions.

clue.text: Run over airy tribute

parts.note: to fly is to run away, flee
past means over, finished, as in the danger is past

explanation.surface: Someone runs over a light-hearted tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airy' means in the air: the tribute is aircraft flying in formation.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial formation of aircraft passing overhead honours an occasion, a salute delivered through the air.

clue.text: Realistic opportunity to keep playing — my Facebook response?

parts.note: in video games an extra life lets you carry on playing
on Facebook you respond to a post by clicking like

explanation.surface: A gamer reacts online to getting another go.
explanation.definitionFit: Something realistic closely resembles the real thing, as a convincing portrait does.

clue.text: Being blunt after misuse no bit can bore into piece of wood

indicators.note: can bore into means the jumbled letters drill into the middle of the wood

parts.note: a plank is a long flat piece of wood

indicators.note: after misuse says the letters of no bit have been mishandled into a new order

explanation.surface: A worn drill bit can still bore through wood once it has gone blunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunt' tempts you towards a dull tool, but it means frank. 'after misuse' jumbles the letters to OINTB, and 'can bore into' drills them in after the first letter of the wood. The entry spans two lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that is direct and frank, with no softening, is described by this phrase for close range.

clue.text: Top missing, letter's incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete says only part of the run missing letter's is used, the answer sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A letter is incomplete because its top part is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like part of the sentence about a missing piece, but it is the definition: a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless vest worn by athletes is a kind of top, the garment for the upper body.

clue.text: Fearful sort of hospital, 10

parts.note: craven means cowardly, fearful
a cottage hospital is a small rural hospital

explanation.surface: A nervous kind of hospital, with a cross-reference attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is GROUND, the first part of 10-across. Craven Cottage is the London home stadium of Fulham Football Club.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-referenced word means a sports stadium, and this is Fulham's football stadium beside the Thames.

clue.text: Pioneering way to make dog run?

parts.note: the clue's last two words dog run use the letters of a six-letter word for earth

explanation.surface: Someone invents a new method to get a dog moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: break up the word GROUND and you get DOG RUN. The answer occupies 10-across and 18-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Innovative work that opens up a new field is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Hoods and collars worn by Scot

indicators.note: worn by means the collars go round the Scot, so his name sits inside them

parts.note: ruffs are frilled Elizabethan collars
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: Hoods and collars form a Scotsman's outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoods' looks like garments to go with collars; it is slang for thugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoods is slang for hoodlums, violent thugs or toughs.

clue.text: State proposal that's acceptable to audience

indicators.note: to audience means the word is heard rather than read, in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: a goer is a proposal that will work and gets the go-ahead

explanation.surface: Declaring an offer that listeners will accept.
explanation.walkthrough: In southern British speech the final R of the word for a workable proposal is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest state of India, on the west coast, a former Portuguese colony.

clue.text: Light reader

definitions.meaning: to light is to set on fire, ignite
Amazon's e-book device is a reader for digital books

explanation.surface: A book that is easy reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite a fire is one sense; the other is the brand name of Amazon's electronic reading device.

clue.text: Oval-shaped ceramic not lasting long

indicators.note: shaped says the letters of oval are formed into a new arrangement

parts.note: a tile is a ceramic square

explanation.surface: An oval ceramic object that does not survive long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oval-shaped' reads as a description of the ceramic, but 'shaped' is the anagram signal, making VOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something volatile is unstable and fleeting, liable to evaporate or change quickly.

clue.text: Tube not sufficiently fine?

parts.note: under as a prefix means not enough, as in undercooked
coffee that is fine has been milled to a powder

explanation.surface: A pipe that is not quite fine enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's metro railway. The answer occupies 15-across and 10-across.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tube is the familiar British name for the London metro railway system.

clue.text: Drink — don't go straight to snack

parts.note: to snake is to wind about rather than move in a line
a bite is a quick snack

explanation.surface: A drinker is told to go straight to a snack instead of wandering.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakebite is a British pub drink of lager mixed with cider.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub mix of lager and cider, sometimes with blackcurrant, is a drink of this name.

clue.text: Wretched folk acquire a place in Ireland

parts.note: bally is an old British euphemism for bloody, damned, wretched
men are people, folk

explanation.surface: Miserable people acquire a spot in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bally' is dated British slang, a softened 'bloody'.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland, is a place on the island of Ireland.

clue.text: Rendering pencil unusable, that's when one loses it

definitions.meaning: snapping a pencil's sharpened tip leaves it unable to write
the moment one loses one's temper or self-control

explanation.surface: Snapping your pencil is the last straw.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer occupies 18-down and 7-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the moment stress becomes too much and someone loses control, and literally snapping a pencil's tip.

clue.text: Not where housekeeper stores the fizzy drinks?

definitions.text: Not where housekeeper stores the fizzy drinks?

parts.words: Not where housekeeper stores the fizzy drinks?
parts.note: a room for non-fizzy drinks would be named after the opposite of sparkling, which is also the name of a housekeeper's storeroom

explanation.surface: A question about where a housekeeper keeps fizzy drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Still drinks are not fizzy, so a room for them would be a still room; a stillroom is really a big house's pantry or distilling room.
explanation.definitionFit: In a large country house, the housekeeper's storeroom for preserves and cordials, once used for distilling.

clue.text: Turn over in half a bikini? Bad girl!

indicators.note: in means the word for turning over goes inside the bikini half

parts.note: a bikini has two halves, top and bottom
to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: Someone rolls over wearing only half a bikini and is scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half a bikini' is not half the letters of BIKINI but one of its two garments, the TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated insult for a promiscuous or slovenly woman, a so-called bad girl.

clue.text: Complete freedom to ignore what may be drawn

parts.note: to blank someone is to ignore them
a bank draft is drawn on an account, as a payment order is

explanation.surface: Total liberty to disregard what someone might sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' suggests sketching, but here it is money drawn on a bank. The answer occupies 21-across and 29-across.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlimited authority to act as one likes, like a signed payment slip with no amount filled in.

clue.text: After fighting, you finally return to rear

indicators.note: after fighting suggests the letters have been battered about into a new order
finally picks the closing letter of you

explanation.surface: A soldier comes home to the rear after battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After fighting' rearranges U and RETURN together.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to bring them up, care for and raise them.

clue.text: Shining example of slogan encouraging more criminals?

definitions.meaning: a guiding light that others follow
split into three words the answer is a recruiting call to become a swindler

explanation.surface: A model campaign line urging people into crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE A CON, the answer is a recruiting slogan for crooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A guiding light or inspiring model for others is a figurative signal fire.

clue.text: Holding head up, lying with pained expression in slang

indicators.note: in means the cry of pain sits inside the word for slang

parts.note: cant is the jargon or slang of a group
ouch is what you say when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone lies down with their head up, groaning in slang.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a heraldic term for a beast lying with its head raised.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, an animal depicted lying down with its head lifted is so described.

clue.text: Order grinder attached to front of cement mixer

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of cement

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
a pounder pounds or grinds things

explanation.surface: Ordering a grinding machine to be fixed to a cement mixer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cement mixer' looks like a single machine, but 'mixer' alone is the definition. The answer occupies 25-down and 15-across.
explanation.definitionFit: One who combines ingredients into a whole, as a pharmacist blends drugs, is a mixer.

clue.text: Friend to bear every journey with constant interruptions

indicators.note: constant interruptions means every other letter is broken off, keeping the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A companion helps a bear on every trip, though they keep getting interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: The bear is Winnie-the-Pooh, whose gloomy donkey friend is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In A. A. Milne's stories the gloomy donkey is a companion of the bear Winnie-the-Pooh.

clue.text: Muslim official, a polytheist at heart

indicators.note: at heart means only the core of the word for polytheist is kept, losing its outer letters

parts.note: a pagan worships many gods

explanation.surface: A Muslim dignitary who secretly believes in many gods.
explanation.definitionFit: A title for a commander or chief in the Ottoman Empire, a Muslim official.

clue.text: Fruit and wine store getting good trade

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
a bin is a rack for storing wine

explanation.surface: A shop selling fruit and wine does good business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trade' looks like commerce, but it is a craft: a plumber's.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting pipes and water systems is a skilled trade, the craft of the plumber.

clue.text: Charlie for one, say, with 7

parts.note: the Berlin Wall crossing was called Checkpoint Charlie; this word sounds like its first part, and 7 supplies the rest

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie, for instance, alongside a number.
explanation.walkthrough: With 7-down (POINT), a word sounding like the answer gives Checkpoint, and Checkpoint Charlie was the famous Berlin Wall crossing. The 'say' signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Its sound-alike check, joined to the next light's word, names the border crossing for which Charlie was one example.

clue.text: In small house, parking is a bit of a mess

indicators.note: In means the parking letter goes inside the small house

parts.note: a lodge is a small house, as at an estate gate
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Parking in a little house makes things messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts P inside S + LODGE, after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot or smear of ink or paint is a small messy mark.

clue.text: In theory, propane is explosive

indicators.note: is explosive suggests the letters of propane are blown apart and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Theoretically the fuel gas can blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means as theory or the written plan says, not necessarily in practice.
